name: Hick's Law
axiom: Decision time increases logarithmically with the number and informational complexity of available choices.
trigger: Users stall or scan repeatedly when a menu or settings page presents many flat, unranked options.

checklist.text: Cap flat options in top-level navigation; each added option lengthens the decision.
Group large select menus into categories or a filterable combobox.
Pre-highlight a recommended default to skip part of the decision tree.

antiPattern.violation: An enterprise settings page offers a flat, unordered dropdown of 85 country options.
antiPattern.remediation: Replace it with an autocomplete combobox: locale auto-detect, keyboard filtering, common options first.

academicOrigin.title: On the Rate of Gain of Information
